items.t: Prophylaxis and treatment of iron deficiency, and prophylaxis of folic acid deficiency, during pregnancy.

src.q: Fefol is a haematinic preparation for prophylaxis and treatment of iron deficiency and prophylaxis of folic acid deficiency during pregnancy.

restrictions.note: No prescribing restrictions in the UK SmPC (MHRA Products, PL 48669/0001).

items.t: Adults only: 1 capsule a day during pregnancy. Some women may need a higher iron dose.

src.q: Adults only: one capsule a day during pregnancy.
Some pregnant patients may need a higher dose of iron because of dietary or other factors.

items.t: Not recommended in children (or in the elderly).

src.q: Children and elderly: not recommended.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to any ingredient.

src.q: Hypersensitivity to any ingredients in the formulation

items.t: Repeated blood transfusions; concomitant parenteral iron; haemochromatosis and other iron overload syndromes.

src.q: patients receiving repeated blood transfusions; concomitant parenteral iron; haemochromatosis and other iron overload syndromes.

items.t: Use with caution in haemolytic anaemia, haemoglobinopathies, iron storage or iron absorption diseases, and existing gastrointestinal disease.

src.q: Administer with caution in patients with haemolytic anaemia, haemoglobinopathies, iron storage or iron absorption diseases, existing gastrointestinal disease.

items.t: Failure to respond may mean another cause of anaemia: investigate. The folic acid content is unlikely to mask pernicious anaemia.

src.q: Failure to respond to treatment may indicate other causes of anaemia and should be further investigated.
The folic acid content is unlikely to mask pernicious anaemia should this condition be present

items.t: Swallow whole: sucking or chewing can cause mouth ulcers and tooth discolouration. Elderly patients and those with swallowing disorders may be at risk of oesophageal lesions or bronchial necrosis if the capsule goes the wrong way.

src.q: Due to the risk of mouth ulcerations and tooth discolouration, capsules should not be sucked, chewed or kept in the mouth, but swallowed whole with water.
Elderly patients and patients with deglutition disorders may also be at risk of oesophageal lesions or of bronchial necrosis, in case of false route.

items.t: Contains sucrose: people with hereditary galactose or fructose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrase-isomaltase insufficiency should not take it.

src.q: Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance or fructose intolerance, the Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrase-isomaltase insufficiency should not take this medicinal product.

items.t: Antacids, zinc, calcium, phosphorus, trientine, tea, coffee, milk, eggs and whole grains reduce iron absorption: do not take iron within 1 hour before or 2 hours after them.

src.q: The absorption of iron salts is also decreased in the presence of antacids, preparations containing zinc, calcium, phosphorus, trientine, or when taken with tea, coffee, milk, eggs and whole grains.
Iron supplements should not be taken within one hour before or two hours after ingestion of these products.

items.t: Oral iron reduces levothyroxine absorption: give at least 2 hours apart (levothyroxine SmPC: 4-5 hours).

src.q: Thyroid hormones: Oral iron reduces the absorption of levothyroxine (thyroxine) thus should be given at least 2 hours apart.
(administration should be separated by 4-5 hours)

items.t: Oral iron reduces absorption of ciprofloxacin, norfloxacin, ofloxacin and bisphosphonates. Ciprofloxacin SmPC: give ciprofloxacin 1-2 hours before or at least 4 hours after iron.

src.q: The absorption of ciprofloxacin, norfloxacin and ofloxacin and bisphosphonates is reduced by oral iron.
ciprofloxacin should be administered either 1-2 hours before or at least 4 hours after these preparations

items.t: Taking iron and tetracyclines together may reduce absorption of both.

src.q: Concurrent administration with tetracyclines may impair absorption of both agents.

items.t: Iron salts may reduce the bioavailability of methyldopa; absorption of levodopa and penicillamine may be reduced.

src.q: Iron salts may reduce the bioavailability of methyldopa. The absorption of levodopa and penicillamine may be reduced.

items.t: Colestyramine may bind iron. Avoid iron with dimercaprol. Ascorbic acid and meat increase iron absorption.

src.q: Cholestyramine may bind iron to the gastrointestinal tract, thus preventing its absorption.
Dimercaprol: Avoid the concomitant use of iron with dimercaprol.
Absorption of iron salts is enhanced by ascorbic acid and meat.

renal.note: No renal impairment advice in the UK SmPC (MHRA Products, PL 48669/0001).

hepatic.note: No hepatic impairment advice in the UK SmPC (MHRA Products, PL 48669/0001).

items.t: Indicated in pregnancy. No known hazards from folic acid in pregnancy; ferrous salts are recommended in pregnancy.

src.q: There are no known hazards to the use of folic acid in pregnancy, supplements of folic acid are often beneficial.
Ferrous salts are recommended for use in pregnancy and lactation, and no contraindications to such are known.

items.t: Ferrous salts are recommended in lactation. Folic acid passes into breast milk; no adverse effects seen in breastfed infants.

src.q: Ferrous salts are recommended for use in pregnancy and lactation, and no contraindications to such are known.
No adverse effects have been observed in breast fed infants whose mothers were receiving folic acid.

reproductive.note: No fertility or contraception statements in the UK SmPC (MHRA Products, PL 48669/0001).

items.t: Gastrointestinal irritation, nausea, vomiting, epigastric pain, diarrhoea (large doses); constipation with continued use, especially in older people; black stools.

src.q: Large doses may produce gastrointestinal irritation, nausea, vomiting, epigastric pain, diarrhoea.
Constipation may be caused by continual administration, particularly in older patients, and may lead to faecal impaction.
Iron supplementation may cause the blackening of stool.

items.t: Hypersensitivity reactions, from rashes (sometimes severe) to anaphylaxis.

src.q: Hypersensitivity reactions have been reported. These range from rashes, sometimes severe, to anaphylaxis.

items.t: Iron overdose is particularly dangerous to young children and is a medical emergency (desferrioxamine is the specific chelator). Keep out of reach of children.

src.q: Overdosage of ferrous salts is particularly dangerous to young children.
Keep out of reach and sight of children, as overdose may be fatal.

items.t: If there is no response, investigate other causes of anaemia.

src.q: Failure to respond to treatment may indicate other causes of anaemia and should be further investigated.

items.t: Swallow whole with water; do not suck, chew or keep in the mouth. Take before or during meals depending on stomach tolerance.

src.q: The capsules should not be sucked, chewed or kept in the mouth, but swallowed whole with water. Capsules should be taken before meals or during meals, depending on gastrointestinal tolerance.

items.t: Stools may turn black. Keep away from children: iron overdose can be fatal.
